job.title: Theatre Services Manager
job.description:
Some leadership roles are about fixing what is broken. 
This isn’t one of them.

This is an opportunity to step into a well established, high performing theatre service where the team is engaged, the culture is positive and the department is humming.

The current Theatre Services Manager has been promoted internally into the General Manager role - creating a rare opportunity to inherit a strong service with continuity, support and genuine momentum.

You’ll lead 7 operating theatres, 6 direct reports and approximately 65 staff across a diverse range of surgical specialties. Orthopaedics is a significant strength, with further growth underway across gynaecology, ophthalmology and robotic surgery.

New contracts have been secured. New surgeons are joining. A robotic surgery programme is developing. The foundations are firmly in place, and the opportunity now is to build on them.

A manager first. A clinician second.

There is considerable clinical expertise within this team. They don’t need someone to be the strongest clinician in every room - they need an experienced manager who can bring people, performance and operations together.

You’ll provide direction to an established group of theatre leaders, maintain strong relationships with surgeons and anaesthetists and ensure the service continues to deliver exceptional patient care while meeting its operational and commercial objectives.

This is a broad leadership role encompassing:
  • Theatre performance, utilisation and operational efficiency
  • Leadership and development of the perioperative team
  • Workforce planning, engagement and performance
  • Budget management and resource allocation
  • Quality, risk, infection prevention and health and safety
  • Strong relationships with surgeons, anaesthetists and internal stakeholders
  • Service development and delivery of future growth initiatives
You’ll report to a supportive General Manager who knows the service exceptionally well, having successfully led the theatre department herself. You’ll also join a collaborative and highly regarded senior leadership team.

Who will thrive here? You’ll be a credible perioperative leader who understands the unique demands of a busy theatre environment, but your real strength will be management. You’ll know how to empower capable clinical leaders, create clarity, make sound decisions and maintain high standards without needing to control every detail. You’ll be commercially aware, comfortable managing budgets and confident building trusted relationships with specialists and senior stakeholders.

You will also bring:
  • Current registration with the Nursing Council of New Zealand
  • At least five years’ experience as a Registered Nurse
  • A minimum of three years’ operating theatre experience
  • Previous people leadership and management experience
  • Experience managing budgets and stakeholder relationships
  • A sound understanding of New Zealand nursing legislation and theatre best practice
  • A collaborative, organised and resilient leadership style
What’s on offer? Alongside a salary of $160,000–$165,000, this role is eligible for a short-term performance incentive and includes:
  • Monday-to-Friday working hours
  • A strong and supportive leadership team
  • A genuinely positive and well-established team culture
  • Two insurance policies
  • Free onsite parking
  • Birthday leave
  • Long-service bonuses
  • Christmas shutdown period
  • Employee benefits, perks and discounts
  • Professional development and conference leave
For someone who wants the scale and professional challenge of leading a substantial surgical service, without inheriting a department in crisis, this is an exceptional opportunity!

The team is strong. The service is growing. The next chapter is ready to be led.

Apply through RWR Health or contact Jeanette Rendle, Agency Director ph 027 705 7079 for a confidential conversation.

Permanent & Fixed-Term | Full-time & Part-time Options | $100,000 - $115,000 + Benefits

Our client is one of New Zealand's largest and most recognised pharmacy networks, delivering accessible healthcare through more than 45 community pharmacies nationwide. About You

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills

Whether you're an experienced Pharmacist looking for your next step or seeking a workplace that offers greater support and long-term career opportunities, we'd love to hear from you.

Benefits & Why You'll Love Working Here

This organisation understands that attracting great Pharmacists is about far more than salary alone. Alongside a competitive remuneration package of $100,000-$115,000, you'll enjoy an outstanding range of benefits designed to support both your career and wellbeing.

  • Ongoing investment in clinical education and professional development
  • Regular salary reviews and annual Short Term Incentive (STI) bonus
  • Genuine Career Progression - many of the organisation's Pharmacy Support Managers, Operations Managers and Category Managers began their careers as community Pharmacists.
  • Share Purchase Plan
  • Grocery discounts of up to 10%
  • Discounted health insurance, dental, optometry and gym memberships

Most importantly, you'll join an organisation where Pharmacists are respected for the contribution they make every day. You'll be supported by experienced leaders, surrounded by collaborative colleagues and encouraged to continually grow your skills while making a meaningful difference to your community.

Whether you're looking to specialise, reduce the demands of shift work, or enjoy the flexibility of working from home, this opportunity offers a rewarding next step in your career.

As an ADHD Assessment Lead, you'll conduct comprehensive adult ADHD assessments using structured clinical interviews, validated assessment tools, and evidence-based practice.

Working within a highly collaborative multidisciplinary team, you'll provide compassionate, patient-centred care while developing specialist expertise in ADHD diagnosis and treatment planning.

You'll enjoy the autonomy of working from home while remaining closely supported by experienced Psychiatrists, General Practitioners, Nurse Practitioners, and an experienced operational team.

You'll bring:
  • Current Nurse Practitioner registration with the Nursing Council of New Zealand
  • Current Annual Practising Certificate
  • Minimum two years' experience as a Nurse Practitioner
  • Strong assessment and clinical decision-making skills
  • Excellent communication and report writing ability
  • Confidence working autonomously
  • A compassionate and patient-centred approach
  • Confidence using telehealth and digital healthcare platforms
Previous ADHD experience is not required.

What You'll Gain
This isn't just another Nurse Practitioner role—it's an opportunity to build specialist expertise while enjoying flexibility rarely found in clinical practice.
You'll benefit from:
  • Fully remote work from anywhere in New Zealand
  • Comprehensive specialist ADHD training
  • A supportive multidisciplinary team
  • Minimal administration through purpose-built technology
  • Ongoing mentoring and professional development
  • Opportunities to contribute to service innovation
  • The chance to genuinely change lives through earlier diagnosis and treatment
Culture & Environment
You'll be joining a passionate team driven by one simple goal—making high-quality ADHD assessment and treatment more accessible for New Zealanders.
The organisation is known for:

  • Collaborative multidisciplinary practice
  • Patient-first care

job.title: Clinical Improvement Lead
job.description:
CLINICAL IMPROVEMENT LEAD | CLINICAL GOVERNANCE & QUALITY
Auckland Central | Youth Mental Health | Clinical Leadership

Lead clinical governance, quality improvement and risk frameworks for a nationally recognised organisation supporting young people across Aotearoa.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

RWR Health is partnering with Youthline, a highly regarded national youth mental health and wellbeing organisation to appoint an experienced Clinical Improvement Lead.

This is an influential, organisation-wide position for a senior registered clinician who wants to shape clinical quality beyond an individual caseload. You will strengthen clinical governance, lead continuous improvement initiatives and provide trusted clinical advice across service delivery, organisational projects and strategic decision-making.

Working alongside executive leaders, service managers and clinical teams, you will help ensure clinical services remain safe, evidence-informed, responsive and aligned with professional standards.

With no direct reports. Its influence comes through clinical credibility, collaboration and the ability to turn governance and quality frameworks into meaningful improvements in practice.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR
  • Leading the implementation, monitoring and ongoing development of the Clinical Governance Framework
  • Supporting or leading the Clinical Governance and Quality Committees
  • Reviewing clinical systems, processes and services to identify risks, gaps and opportunities for improvement
  • Developing and implementing practical quality and service-improvement initiatives
  • Providing senior clinical advice for complex, critical and high-risk situations
  • Strengthening clinical risk-assessment, escalation and incident-management processes
  • Advising on policy development, service design, funding applications and strategic projects
  • Monitoring clinical quality data, emerging risks, trends and improvement outcomes
  • Facilitating clinical meetings, reflective practice and professional-development activities
  • Developing training and resources across clinical governance, risk, quality and best practice
  • Building engagement with clinical governance and continuous improvement across the organisation
ABOUT YOU
You will be a credible and experienced clinician who can work comfortably across frontline practice, governance and organisational strategy. You will bring sound judgement, strong facilitation skills and the ability to influence people outside formal reporting lines.

You will ideally offer:
  • Significant clinical experience, including exposure to complex or high-risk environments
  • Experience in clinical governance, clinical quality, risk or continuous improvement
  • Experience developing, implementing or reviewing clinical frameworks and service-improvement initiatives
  • Strong leadership, facilitation and project-management capability
  • Confidence supporting complex clinical decisions and escalation processes
  • Strong knowledge of clinical, ethical, legislative and regulatory requirements
  • Excellent written communication, with the ability to contribute to policies, reports, funding applications and strategic initiatives
  • A collaborative, analytical and solutions-focused approach
  • Experience within youth, community, mental health or telehealth services would be highly valued
  • Knowledge and experience supporting Māori, Pacific, Rainbow, Asian and other priority communities would be advantageous
REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS

You must hold a relevant tertiary clinical qualification and be fully registered with a recognised New Zealand professional or membership body under the HCPA Act such as SWRB, NZAC, NZNO, NZCCA, DAPAANZ or NZAP etc.

WHY CONSIDER THIS ROLE?

This is an opportunity to move beyond managing a single clinical service and contribute to quality and safety across an entire organisation.
You’ll have the scope to influence governance, policy, capability, service design and clinical decision-making while supporting an organisation with a strong purpose and a longstanding commitment to improving outcomes for rangatahi.

job.title: Clinical Quality & Project Specialist
job.description:
CLINICAL QUALITY & PROJECT SPECIALIST | YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY
Are you a registered mental health clinician who is naturally drawn to improving how services work, not just delivering them?

RWR Health is seeking a Clinical Quality & Project Specialist for Youthline, a  respected national youth mental health and wellbeing organisation based in Auckland Central.

This is a varied, hands-on position sitting between clinical practice, quality improvement and project delivery. You will review clinical practice, identify opportunities for improvement and help turn those insights into stronger policies, training, systems and services.

You will work closely with Helpline leadership, service managers, clinical teams and the wider Quality Improvement Team to support safe, consistent and evidence-informed care for rangatahi and other clients.

Unlike a purely administrative quality role, this position retains a connection to frontline service delivery. You will contribute to case management, clinical guidance and the nationwide 24/7 Helpline, including supporting occasional coverage requirements.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR
  • Reviewing and monitoring clinical practice against policy, procedure and best-practice standards
  • Identifying quality, training and service-development opportunities
  • Supporting clinical quality monitoring and governance processes
  • Helping services remain audit-ready through accurate and timely quality controls
  • Contributing to clinical incident reviews and improvement recommendations
  • Supporting the development and review of policies, procedures and clinical guidelines
  • Leading and supporting quality-improvement projects from design through to implementation and evaluation
  • Driving service innovation across Helpline, therapy and youth-development services
  • Contributing clinical expertise to workforce training and development
  • Supporting reflective practice, clinical debriefing and Helpline meetings
  • Contributing to case management and clear, person-centred care planning
  • Maintaining accurate clinical and quality information across client-management systems
  • Supporting the nationwide Helpline when required
ABOUT YOU

You will be an experienced, fully registered clinician who combines sound clinical judgement with curiosity about how services can be made safer, more consistent and more effective.
You will bring:
  • Proven mental health experience, ideally involving young people and whānau
  • Demonstrated quality-improvement or service-development experience
  • The ability to translate research and evidence into practical clinical improvements
  • Confidence identifying and prioritising clinical risk
  • The ability to make timely, sound decisions using best-practice clinical standards
  • Experience engaging clients, families, whānau and community stakeholders
  • Strong reflective practice and a calm, non-judgemental approach
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence managing competing priorities in a responsive service environment
  • The ability to lead, coach, provide feedback and support workforce development
  • A genuine commitment to improving outcomes for young people
  • Telehealth, Helpline or crisis-service experience would be advantageous
REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS
To be considered, you must hold a current Annual Practising Certificate and be fully registered in New Zealand as one of the following:
  • A health practitioner registered under the HPCA Act, such as a nurse, psychologist, psychotherapist or occupational therapist etc.
  • A registered alcohol and drug or gambling practitioner with DAPAANZ
  • A fully registered social worker
  • A counsellor fully registered with NZAC
You must also have relevant clinical experience within mental health, ideally including youth mental health or addiction services.

WHY THIS ROLE?
This position offers a rare combination of direct clinical connection and broader organisational impact.
You will be able to see what is happening in practice, identify what could work better and then help design and implement the solution. Your work will influence clinical quality, workforce capability, service innovation and the experience of rangatahi accessing support.

job.title: Helpline Support Worker
job.description:
Do you have a passion for supporting rangatahi and want to make a meaningful impact through direct crisis intervention and clinical support? This is your opportunity to work with Youthline’s Helpline Services Team in a structured, high-impact role.

About the Role
As a Helpline Support Worker, you’ll be on the frontline providing essential support to young people accessing Youthline’s Helpline through text, phone, email, and webchat. You’ll also be a key support to Helpline Volunteers, providing mentoring, clinical guidance, and helping to manage risk in real-time.
This is a permanent, full-time role on a 4x4 roster (four days on, four days off).
  • Evening shifts (6:00pm - Midnight)
You’ll need to be confident in risk assessment, decision-making, and coaching others - often autonomously.
Key Responsibilities:
  • Deliver person-centred, strength-based support to Helpline clients
  • Provide clinical leadership and mentoring to Helpline Volunteers
  • Conduct and guide risk assessments and escalate as required
  • Maintain quality documentation and contribute to continuous improvement
  • Support a positive, inclusive, and safe team environment
What You’ll Bring:
  • Registration under the HPCA Act, NZAC, DAPAANZ, or SWRB
  • Experience in a mental health, counselling, or crisis support role
  • Strong risk assessment and clinical decision-making skills
  • Empathy, emotional regulation, and the ability to lead under pressure
  • Experience working in telehealth is highly desirable
What’s on Offer:
  • The chance to make a direct impact on the wellbeing of rangatahi in Aotearoa
  • A strong clinical team culture with support and supervision
  • Hybrid working structure offering both in-office and remote shifts
  • Work for a mission-driven organisation deeply rooted in community
This is a vital, rewarding position for someone who thrives in high-trust environments and believes in the power of connection, whanaungatanga, and youth-led support.

Apply Today!!

Located just minutes from the beach, this is an opportunity to combine a rewarding pharmacy career with everything the Bay of Plenty has to offer, from morning walks along the coastline to an active outdoor lifestyle and a welcoming community.

Whether you're already based in the region or considering a lifestyle move, this role offers the opportunity to grow your career without compromising on work-life balance.

Your responsibilities will include:

Career Development
  • Ongoing professional development and funded learning opportunities
  • Genuine career progression within one of New Zealand's leading pharmacy organisations
  • Supportive leadership focused on helping you achieve your career goals
Work-Life Balance
  • Collaborative rostering with flexibility wherever possible to support your lifestyle and personal commitments
  • Supportive team environment that values wellbeing as much as performance
Additional Benefits
  • Staff discounts across one of New Zealand's leading retail groups
  • Additional savings on selected products

job.title: Psychologist
job.description:
Registered Psychologist | Timaru

Join a collaborative rehabilitation team where your expertise helps people rebuild their lives after injury.

An exciting opportunity is available for a Registered Psychologist or Clinical Psychologist to join a well-established multidisciplinary rehabilitation provider in Timaru. Whether you're looking for full-time or part-time work (minimum 15 hours per week), you'll become part of a supportive team with an established caseload and strong clinical leadership.

This role offers meaningful work with clients recovering from a wide range of injuries, alongside excellent professional development and genuine work-life balance.
The Opportunity Working primarily within ACC-funded rehabilitation, you'll support clients who have experienced traumatic injuries and require psychological assessment and intervention as part of their recovery.
Your caseload will include clients experiencing:
  • Chronic pain
  • Concussion and mild traumatic brain injury
  • Trauma following injury
  • Sensitive Claims
  • Mental health impacts of injury
  • Return-to-work and vocational rehabilitation needs
Every day is different. You'll manage your own diary and caseload, conducting psychological assessments, providing evidence-based therapy, preparing comprehensive reports, and working closely with a multidisciplinary team to help clients achieve the best possible outcomes.
Most assessments are completed from the Timaru clinic, with occasional home visits where reasonable adjustments are required.
About You We're looking for a Registered Psychologist or Clinical Psychologist who enjoys working collaboratively and is passionate about supporting people through recovery.

You'll ideally bring:
  • Registration (or eligibility for registration) with the New Zealand Psychologists Board
  • Around three years' or more post-registration experience
  • Strong psychological assessment and report writing skills
  • Experience working within rehabilitation, injury, or ACC environments
  • An interest or experience in pain management and concussion rehabilitation (highly desirable, but not essential)
Applications are also welcomed from overseas psychologists who are eligible to obtain New Zealand registration.
Why Join? You'll be joining a close-knit team with an excellent reputation for collaboration and staff retention. You'll work alongside experienced psychologists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, nurses, counsellors and administration staff, with support from an experienced Team Leader who understands the role firsthand.

What's on offer
  • Salary of $85,000-$105,000, depending on experience
  • Full-time or part-time opportunities (minimum 15 hours per week)
  • 5 weeks annual leave
  • $2,500 annual professional development allowance
  • Up to $2,000 relocation assistance
  • Established caseload from day one
  • Low staff turnover and supportive team culture
  • Genuine multidisciplinary approach to client care
  • Opportunities to further develop your skills in concussion, pain management and complex psychological assessment
If you're looking for a varied role where you can make a real difference while being supported by an experienced and collaborative team, we'd love to hear from you.

Know someone suitable? We offer a $500 referral bonus for successful referrals.

job.title: Clinical Manager
job.description:
Clinical Manager | Aged Care Christchurch | $105,000-$125,000 

Ready to take the next step in your aged care leadership career?

Whether you're an experienced Clinical Manager looking for your next challenge or an accomplished Unit Coordinator ready to step into your first Clinical Manager position, this could be the opportunity you've been waiting for.
We're partnering with a well-established aged care provider in Christchurch to recruit a Clinical Manager for their 144-bed facility. You'll join a collaborative leadership team where you'll be supported by an experienced Facility Manager with over 30 years in aged care and healthcare, alongside another Clinical Manager who works closely with you to ensure exceptional resident care.
About the Role This modern aged care facility provides Rest Home and Hospital level care, including a dedicated 16-bed Younger Person with Disabilities (YPD) service.

As one of two Clinical Managers, you'll oversee either the Hospital or Rest Home service, rotating portfolios every three months. This unique structure allows both leaders to build strong relationships across the entire facility while developing a broad understanding of all aspects of the service.

The Clinical Managers work opposite rosters to ensure strong leadership coverage:

On-call responsibilities are shared and light, averaging one week in every three.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Drive high-quality clinical care and positive resident outcomes

  • Mentor and develop nursing staff
  • Ensure compliance with aged care standards and clinical governance requirements

What's on Offer

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
Lead one of New Zealand's premier retirement communities into its next chapter
  • Outstanding opportunity for a commercially astute leader
  • Lead a significant, multi-faceted retirement community
  • Report to and work closely with the Board of Directors
About the organisation

Nestled across 12 hectares in beautiful Gisborne, Beetham Lifestyle Village is one of New Zealand's premium resort style retirement communities. Home to 161 villas and 12 serviced apartments it also incorporates Beetham Healthcare - a 48 bed aged care facility. Privately owned, Beetham has earned an outstanding reputation for its welcoming community, exceptional care and a strong organisational culture.

Following the planned retirement of their long serving General Manager, we are seeking an experienced leader to guide the village through its next stage of growth and success.

This is an outstanding opportunity for a commercially astute leader who enjoys balancing strategy with hands on leadership while making a genuine difference to the lives of residents, families and staff.

About the Job

You will report to and work closely with the Board of Directors providing strategic and operational leadership across the organisation and ensuring strong commercial performance while preserving the outstanding culture Beetham is renowned for.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading a significant, multi-faceted retirement community.
  • Driving village occupancy, sales and long term growth.
  • Managing financial performance, budgets, forecasting and KPIs.
  • Developing and delivering strategic business plans.
  • Building trusted relationships with residents, families, staff and stakeholders.
  • Supporting and developing a high performing leadership team.
  • Working closely with an engaged and forward thinking Board.
About You
We're seeking an experienced General Manager or senior leader with proven commercial and operational leadership experience. You will currently be leading within retirement living or healthcare but we will also consider other complex service based businesses.

You'll bring:
  • Confidence and experience reporting to and working collaboratively with a Board of Directors
  • Demonstrated success leading a significant business or operation.
  • Strong financial acumen with P&L responsibility.
  • Experience improving commercial performance, occupancy or revenue growth.
  • Strategic thinking coupled with operational excellence.
  • An authentic leadership style that builds trust, engagement and high-performing teams.
What's on Offer
  • Salary of $140,000 + depending on experience.
  • Relocation assistance may be available.
  • A comprehensive handover with the outgoing General Manager.
  • The opportunity to shape the future of one of New Zealand's most respected retirement communities.
  • An engaged Board committed to supporting the successful candidate.

Why Gisborne?

Whether you already have a connection to the region or are looking for a lifestyle change, Gisborne offers beautiful beaches, wineries, outdoor adventure and one of New Zealand's warmest climates. It's a place where you can enjoy an exceptional career without compromising on quality of life.

Apply Confidentially

As the exclusive recruitment partner for Beetham Lifestyle Village, RWR Health is managing this appointment on behalf of the Board.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Jeanette Rendle, Agency Director at RWR Health, ph 027 705 7079 or click Apply to submit your application.

All enquiries and applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

We are currently recruiting for an experienced Medical Administrator to join a well-established GP & Urgent Care clinic in Remuera, Auckland.

This is an opportunity to become an important part of the clinic's day-to-day operations, supporting patients, clinicians and the wider administration team across a busy and varied environment.

If you're someone who enjoys being the person others can rely on, takes pride in getting the detail right, and thrives when no two days are quite the same, this could be a great next step.

  • Become a trusted point of support across reception and administration
  • Enjoy a varied role spanning General Practice and Urgent Care
  • Work alongside an experienced and supportive clinical team
  • Monday–Friday focus with occasional Saturday cover

Working across both General Practice and Urgent Care, you'll play an important role in keeping the clinic running efficiently while delivering an excellent experience for patients.

You'll be someone the wider reception team can turn to for support, guidance and problem-solving, while working closely with clinicians and management to ensure the day-to-day operation runs smoothly.

job.title: Psychiatrist
job.description:
About RWR Health
At RWR Health, we are passionate about connecting healthcare professionals with opportunities that genuinely align with their career goals, clinical interests, and lifestyle aspirations.

We take a consultative, long-term approach—partnering with healthcare organisations that value clinical excellence, innovation, and patient-centred care. With strong networks across New Zealand’s healthcare sector, we pride ourselves on connecting exceptional clinicians with organisations where they can truly make a difference.

Consultant Psychiatrist
Remote Work From Anywhere in New Zealand | Flexible Hours | Employee or Contractor

What if you could use your specialist expertise to help improve access to adult ADHD care across New Zealand, without taking on a traditional full-time clinical workload?

RWR Health is proud to partner with an innovative telehealth provider focused on making adult ADHD assessment and treatment more accessible, timely, and patient-centred.

We are seeking an experienced Consultant Psychiatrist to provide specialist clinical oversight to a team of General Practitioners and Nurse Practitioners delivering adult ADHD assessments across New Zealand.

This is an opportunity to use your expertise where it matters most—supporting clinical decision-making, maintaining high standards of care, and helping clinicians deliver safe, consistent and evidence-based ADHD assessments.

Why This Role Stands Out
  • Work remotely from anywhere in New Zealand
  • Flexible hours with employee or contractor options
  • Provide specialist oversight without a high-volume patient caseload
  • Support and develop a multidisciplinary team of GPs and Nurse Practitioners
  • Help shape clinical standards within an innovative telehealth service
  • Minimal administration, with dedicated coordinators managing the operational workload
The Opportunity
As Consultant Psychiatrist, you'll act as the specialist clinical backstop for a growing adult ADHD service.

Your focus will be on reviewing and signing off diagnostic assessments completed by GPs and Nurse Practitioners, providing clinical supervision and acting as a trusted source of specialist advice when complex cases arise.

You'll also chair a weekly multidisciplinary team meeting, ensuring cases are discussed thoroughly and that clear clinical outcomes and next steps are agreed.

Alongside this, you'll contribute to the service's Clinical Governance programme, helping shape protocols, audit processes and ongoing clinical standards.

This is a role for a Psychiatrist who enjoys clinical leadership, collaboration and improving the quality of care, rather than simply delivering consultations.

Your Role You'll be responsible for:
  • Reviewing and providing clinical sign-off for adult ADHD assessments
  • Providing clinical supervision to GP and Nurse Practitioner assessors
  • Supporting clinicians with complex diagnostic and clinical questions
  • Chairing weekly multidisciplinary team meetings
  • Providing specialist input into differential diagnosis and clinical risk
  • Contributing to clinical governance, protocols and audit
  • Supporting consistent, evidence-based clinical standards
  • Promoting culturally safe, patient-centred practice
About You
You are a vocationally registered Psychiatrist with strong experience in adult ADHD who enjoys working collaboratively within a modern, digitally enabled healthcare environment.

You'll bring:
  • Vocational registration in Psychiatry with the Medical Council of New Zealand
  • Current Annual Practising Certificate
  • FRANZCP or recognised equivalent
  • Current medical indemnity insurance
  • Strong understanding of adult ADHD and DSM-5 diagnostic criteria
  • Confidence with stimulant prescribing within the New Zealand healthcare environment
  • Experience providing clinical supervision or specialist clinical guidance
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence working autonomously within a remote environment
You'll also have a genuine commitment to culturally safe practice and the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

Culture & Environment
You'll be joining a growing multidisciplinary team committed to making adult ADHD care more accessible across New Zealand.

The service has been designed around a simple principle: patients shouldn't have to wait years to access quality ADHD assessment and care.
You'll work alongside GPs, Nurse Practitioners and other specialist clinicians within a supportive environment that values:
  • Clinical excellence
  • Collaboration and shared learning
  • Accessible healthcare
  • Evidence-based practice
  • Continuous improvement
  • Patient-centred care
The Flexibility This role has been designed to work around the clinician.
You can:
  • Work entirely remotely
  • Choose flexible working arrangements
  • Engage as an employee or contractor
  • Focus on specialist clinical oversight rather than administration
  • Support a growing national service without committing to a traditional full-time position
Dedicated coordinators manage bookings, forms and patient communication, allowing you to focus on the clinical work that requires your specialist expertise.

Why This Opportunity?
Adult ADHD care in New Zealand is evolving rapidly.
This is an opportunity to be part of that change—providing the clinical leadership and specialist oversight that ensures patients receive safe, high-quality and consistent care.

For a Consultant Psychiatrist looking for flexibility, meaningful clinical influence and the opportunity to help shape a growing service, this is a role worth exploring.

We offer a $500 referral bonus if your referral is successfully placed.

job.title: Clinical Service Leader
job.description:
Are you an experienced Registered Psychologist with a background in harmful sexual behaviour or forensic practice, looking to step into a senior clinical leadership role without moving away from clinical practice?
We are seeking a Clinical Service Lead to provide clinical leadership, guidance and oversight across services throughout Northland, Auckland, Waikato and Tauranga.

You'll be a senior clinical resource for experienced clinicians providing case consultation, reviewing clinical practice, supporting complex decision-making and helping develop the quality and consistency of the Adult Services programme.

The opportunity
Reporting to the Clinical Director, you'll provide clinical leadership across a geographically dispersed team while remaining connected to practice yourself.

A significant part of your role will involve supporting clinicians with their clinical work. You'll hold regular monthly one-to-one meetings, review caseloads, provide guidance around complex presentations and risk, and ensure assessment and intervention approaches remain clinically robust.
You'll also have an opportunity to influence the ongoing development of the Adult Services programme, clinical frameworks and ways of working.

The position description places approximately 60% of the role's focus on clinical leadership, with a further 20% dedicated to clinical work, alongside learning and development and stakeholder engagement.

What you'll be doing
  • Providing clinical leadership and guidance across Adult Services in Northland, Auckland, Waikato and Tauranga
  • Holding monthly clinical 1:1s with clinicians, including reviewing caseloads and providing case consultation
  • Providing specialist guidance on complex presentations, risk, assessment and intervention
  • Reviewing and approving assessment and intervention reports to support consistently high standards of practice
  • Supporting the effective triage of new referrals
  • Providing clinical direction around complex cases, ethical considerations and client risk
  • Supporting clinicians working with specialist populations, including clients with intellectual disabilities and women
  • Contributing to the development and refinement of Safe Network's Adult Services programme
  • Supporting clinical onboarding, capability development and training
  • Contributing to clinical policies, programmes and best-practice frameworks
  • Maintaining a level of hands-on clinical practice, including assessment and therapeutic intervention
  • Building collaborative relationships with referrers, agencies and other sector stakeholders
  • Travelling across the Northern Region as required
The position has no direct reports, so your leadership comes through your clinical expertise, credibility, guidance and ability to positively influence practice.

What we're looking for
We're particularly interested in hearing from experienced psychologists who have worked within harmful sexual behaviour services or forensic environments.
You'll need to be comfortable with some of the more complex presentations encountered within Adult Services and bring well-developed expertise across assessment, risk and therapeutic intervention.
You'll ideally bring:
  • Full registration as a Psychologist with NZPB
  • Relevant clinical experience 
  • Strong experience delivering clinical assessments within harmful sexual behaviour or forensic settings
  • Expertise across harmful sexual behaviour assessment and intervention
  • Experience with systemic interventions and group work
  • Strong risk assessment, formulation and clinical decision-making capability
  • Previous clinical leadership experience
  • Confidence providing consultation, feedback and guidance to experienced clinicians
  • The ability to review complex clinical information and provide clear direction
  • Strong written skills and experience producing or reviewing high-quality clinical reports
  • An ability to build credibility and effective working relationships across geographically dispersed services
  • A collaborative, thoughtful and culturally responsive approach to practice
  • Flexibility to undertake some regional travel
Experience supporting specialist populations, including people with intellectual disabilities would also be valuable.

With a strong focus on creating safer outcomes for individuals, whānau and communities.

This is an opportunity to bring your expertise into a role where you can have a broader clinical impact – supporting other experienced practitioners, strengthening clinical practice and contributing to the future development of specialist Adult Services – without taking on traditional staff-management responsibilities.

What's in it for you?
Alongside the professional opportunity, this role offers a strong benefits package including:
  • Competitive Salary
  • Health insurance
  • Income protection insurance
  • Critical care cover
  • Annual professional registration
  • Monthly professional supervision
  • Car parking
If you're an experienced Registered Psychologist from an HSB, forensic or closely aligned specialist background and want to move into a role where your clinical expertise can influence practice across an entire service, we'd love to hear from you.
